content.body: We could maybe have a <dfn> for "the given value". Forgot why Domenic and I opted not to do that.

It looks to me like Chromium is switching (non-XSLT) XML parsing from libxml2 to https://github.com/kornelski/xml-rs . The README of the crate says that it targets XML 1.1. Is Chromium switching support for Web XML from 1.0 4th ed to 1.1, or are there some changes to keep the target as 1.0 4th ed. despite the README?
Whoa. TIL that 1.0th 5th ed. went this far: https://github.com/kornelski/xml-rs/commit/bd8fe074cca1ed5f1aadaa151284c3d218308484
Was Chromium doing 5th ed. already previously? I thought the Web was 4th ed.
FWIW, libexpat is explicitly 4th ed.
Whoa. https://wpt.fyi/results/xml/xml-prolog-accepted-versions.html?label=master&label=experimental&aligned
I have a recollection of the WHATWG leaning towards staying on 4th ed. Was Chromium's and WebKit's move to 5th ed. discussed here or did it just happen?
The wpt test case appears to come from a hidden Chromium issue: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/441911594
Looks like Chromium was doing this already 13 years ago: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=501837#c5

Ladybird shows the same results as WebKit and Chrome for that

https://wpt.fyi/results/xml/xml-prolog-accepted-versions.html?label=master&product=chrome%5Bexperimental%5D&product=firefox%5Bexperimental%5D&product=safari%5Bexperimental%5D&product=ladybird&aligned

And Ladybird’s just using libxml2 as-is. So I assume that’s from libxml2 behavior as-is.
sideshowbarker: AFAICT, libxml2 has a flag to request 4th ed. behavior, but I guess the browsers that use libxml2 don't set that flag.
content.formatted_body: sideshowbarker: AFAICT, libxml2 has a flag to request 4th ed. behavior, but I guess the browsers that use libxml2 don't set that flag.

content.body: I'm very curious why 5th ed. didn't take the relaxation of the value space of text node content from XML 1.1. That's in practice a much bigger footgun of XML and would have been worthwhile to fix if making a breaking change. Instead, stuff like https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/d34ae755-c53f-4a44-a363-c6dd3ee018a4 had to happen.

Right. I implemented Ladybird’s switch over to libxml2 (away from a custom XML parser LB had until then). And I guess I didn’t even know about that switch. But even if I had, I wouldn’t have used it — because, interop.
hsivonen: pretty sure we knew this was broken and out of sync.

content.body:
Having just needed to look into something around XML, I happened to notice that the normative reference in the HTML standard points to https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/, which is currently 1.0 5th edition.

It seems a bit surprising to me that there isn't alignment on this.
Is that the XML5 I've heard so much about?
we do have a dfn for it, but it's not referenced
https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#the-given-value
I can prepare a PR for a blanket replacement of this (but not before I finish the current PRs)
anyway, this is fixed in the new revision together with everything else, plus better PR commit messages
